capitals.name: Torres (Porto Torres)
capitals.note: 'The first capital city of the Giudicato of Logudoro was ancient Torres'; the seat moved after Arab attacks on the coastal city. The page gives no year for the move: 1099 is the dossier's bridge (confidence 1), placed before the 1132 and 1237 dates at Ardara.

capitals.name: Ardara
capitals.note: the seat later moved to Ardara and then to Sassari (Logudoro page, no years); Ardara 'was one of the capitals of' the Judicate of Torres (Ardara page, coordinates from it). Ardara is dated as a seat only by the Gallura page (Comita I of Gallura did homage there on 26 June 1132) and the Adelasia page (Adelasia swore vassalage to the pope's envoy there in 1237). The later move to Sassari is undated and is not drawn.

keyframe_review.note: unverified for 866-1014: the page has the island split into four provinces only by the 11th century (Logudoro and Arborea were combined at the start of the 11th century) and the judicates de facto independent by 1073; infobox Established: 11th century. The outline is a retrospective district of the later judicate. 8,247 km2; the page gives no infobox area to compare. Soft.

The Taifa of Denia page says the army 'settled a military camp in the north of the island for one year' (1015-1016) and names no judicate. The reduced shape holds for 1015-1016 only; the full shape returns in 1017. The page describes a camp, not a conquest of half the judicate, so the cut-out is Cliopatria's stand-in.
8,247 km2: the north-west of Sardinia, bordering Gallura to the east, Arborea to the south and Cagliari to the south-east, as the page says. Applies from 1017 (see the 1015 verdict). No infobox area.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria has no Logudoro shape for 1066-1071 (its rows run 1018-1065 and 1072-1249). The page has Barisone I reigning 'from about 1038 to 1073' (infobox 1060-1073) and no break, so the gap is a defect of the data. Reviewer 2026-10-25: Cliopatria's Giudicato of Arborea row draws 12,248 km2 for 1066-1071 (shapes.csv giudicato-of-arborea_1066, bbox 8.15-9.43 E, 39.58-41.13 N), that is Arborea's 3,855 km2 plus Logudoro's 8,247 km2: Cliopatria hands Logudoro to Arborea in these years. The Logudoro page combines the two only 'at the start of the 11th century' and has Barisone I reigning to 1073, so this keyframe stands and the Arborea dossier should mark its 1066 shape adjust (minus Logudoro).
8,247 km2 for 1072-1249; the page names curatoriae and neighbours but no boundary, and nothing in the pages opened changes the land before 1259.
Same outline (8,247 km2) with fewer vertices. The judicate ends with Adelasia's death in 1259 (the kingdom ended when Queen Adelasia died without an heir in 1259); the shape matches the end year.

ledger.note: 1259: Adelasia dies without an heir and Logudoro is broken up. She died 'in 1259, without heirs'; her territory was split among the Doria, Malaspina and Spinola families, who held it from Genoa; Arborea gained some land; Sassari became an autonomous city-state allied with Genoa. The Logudoro page agrees on 1259 ('Disestablished: 1259'). The pages give no boundaries between the successors; month not given.

wars.name: Dénia invasion of Sardinia

zones.text: the north of the island, where the Dénia army 'settled a military camp ... for one year' (Taifa of Dénia page); drawn as the part Cliopatria cuts from Logudoro in 1015-1017

wars.outcome: The Dénia army held a camp in the north of Sardinia for one year; the fleets of Pisa and Genoa reconquered the island; Mujahid's heir Ali Iqbal al-Dawla was captured and ransomed only in 1032.
wars.note: The page names no judicate and no date for the reconquest; the Mujahid al-Amiri page puts the occupied land in the south.

wars.name: Genoese and Torres attack on Gallura
wars.outcome: In 1211 Comita III of Torres agreed to a treaty with Genoa to jointly conquer the island, Gallura first; Pisa struck back in 1212; Pope Honorius III forced a settlement on 1 December 1217.
wars.note: Read from the Gallura page; the Logudoro page does not mention it. No ground taken or held is recorded, so no zone and no contest event are written.

certainty.note: No treaty or survey line is on any page opened: the pages give twenty curatoriae and the neighbours' names only, and Cliopatria's outline follows modern provinces. The 1259 partition lines among the Doria, Malaspina, Spinola, Arborea and Sassari are not given.

notes: FOUNDING: Cliopatria starts the row in 866; the page says Established: 11th century and has the island split into four provinces only by the 11th century, with Barisone I reigning 'from about 1038 to 1073' (infobox 1060-1073). The dossier keeps 866 at confidence 1 as Cliopatria's year; a gap-filler may prefer c.1038. GAP IN CLIOPATRIA: no shape 1066-1071, filled by a new keyframe. DENIA: the Taifa of Denia dossier (eu-12) records an occupation of the 'Sardinia intersect Logudoro 1015' remnant; here the hatched land is the part Cliopatria cuts out, since the page says only 'the north of the island'. PERSONAL UNIONS AND OVERLORDS (no territory event written, rule 4): the Logudoro page says Logudoro and Arborea were combined at the start of the 11th century and the Arborea page that in 1145, after Comita was excommunicated, 'the Judicate of Arborea was nominally transferred to Logudoro' (Arborea page); the Gallura page says that in 1236 Logudoro was acquired through marriage to Adelasia, while the Adelasia page has her acclaimed judge in her own right in 1236 (Ubaldo II of Gallura, her husband since 1219, died 1238) and, in 1237, swearing vassalage to Pope Gregory IX's envoy at Ardara, recognizing papal suzerainty over Logudoro (the Papal States dossier should carry the vassal_start for giudicato-of-logudoro). ENZO: the Adelasia page has Enzo, son of Frederick II, marry her in 1238 and be titled King of Sardinia, leaving in 1239 and never returning, the marriage annulled 1245 or 1246: no territory. END: successors are the Genoese families (Doria, Malaspina, Spinola), Arborea and Sassari; Republic of Sassari has no dossier (list under counterparts_needing_dossiers) and the Genoa dossier (eu-13) should carry the matching gain in 1259. CAPITALS: Torres to 1099 is the dossier's bridge (page silent); Sassari as a last seat is not drawn. RULERS: the pages give Barisone I 1060-1073 (text 1038), Marianus II 1218-1233 and Adelasia 1236-1259 with gaps, so no ruler strip is written. Budget: five pages plus the thin Ardara page for the coordinates. No gazetteer name is needed beyond Republic of Sassari as a dossier.
